issue.title: PromQL: make default lookback configurable (query parameter + cluster setting)

labels.name: user-67ce657a/repo-12a517a4
labels.description: PromQL support for Elastic

issue.body:
## Summary
`PromqlCommand` currently hardcodes `DEFAULT_LOOKBACK = 5m` for instant-selector evaluation without an explicit range selector.

## Problem
The default lookback cannot be customized today:
- per query (for specific workloads)
- globally via cluster setting

This makes it hard to tune behavior for sparse/irregular metric streams and Prometheus compatibility expectations.

## Proposed direction
- Add a query-level PromQL parameter for lookback (for example `lookback_delta`).
- Add a cluster setting that defines the default lookback used when the query parameter is not provided.
- Preserve current behavior (`5m`) as the fallback default for compatibility.

## Context
- Review comment: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/149690#discussion_r3298708187
- Existing code TODO: `x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/plan/logical/promql/PromqlCommand.java` (`DEFAULT_LOOKBACK`).

comment.body:
This should also cover changing range queries to use lookback independently of step, rather than only making the existing five-minute constant configurable.

Today, a plain selector such as up uses a fixed five-minute lookback in an instant query, but only looks within the current step-sized bucket in a range query. To match Prometheus, step should control how often we evaluate the expression, while lookback controls how far back each evaluation can select the latest sample. For example, step=30s and lookback_delta=2m should evaluate every 30 seconds and look back two minutes each time. The same sample can appear at several evaluation times until it expires or a newer sample replaces it.

A possible implementation is to give plain selectors an explicit lookback window when translating them to last_over_time, while keeping the evaluation buckets aligned to step. We already have windowed aggregation machinery for explicit expressions such as last_over_time(up[2m]), including filling later buckets that have no new samples. That looks like a useful starting point, rather than introducing a separate execution mechanism. The source timestamp filter must also read back far enough before the first evaluation. Expanding that filter alone would not fix later steps.

The effective lookback should come from the query parameter, then the cluster default, then the five-minute fallback, and apply consistently to instant and range queries. Explicit ranges such as rate(x[1m]) should keep their own windows.

Tests should cover step shorter and longer than lookback, steps with no new samples, expiry at the window boundary, and a single-step range query agreeing with an instant query at the same time. The documented range-query lookback difference should be removed once this is implemented.
Remove this function given its value is inferable from `child()` anyway.

issue.title: [ES|QL] PROMQL on 9.5: rate/irate/increase over a gauge field throw ClassCastException (ReferenceAttribute → Bucket) when the step exceeds the range window

labels.name: user-67ce657a/repo-12a517a4
labels.description: PromQL support for Elastic

issue.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

9.5.3 (also 9.5.0-SNAPSHOT `ca18acd4`, 2026-08-03). Not reproducible on 9.6.0-SNAPSHOT (`eba6e093`, 2026-10-01) or 9.7.0-SNAPSHOT (`679b3d8f`, 2026-10-28).

### Installed Plugins

_none_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Official Docker images on Docker Desktop for macOS (`Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit aarch64`)

### Problem Description

On 9.5.3, PROMQL `rate()`, `irate()` and `increase()` over a field mapped `time_series_metric: gauge` fail with a `class_cast_exception` once the query step is larger than the range-vector window:

```
class_cast_exception: class org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.core.expression.ReferenceAttribute cannot be cast to class org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.expression.function.grouping.Bucket (org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.core.expression.ReferenceAttribute and org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.expression.function.grouping.Bucket are in unnamed module of loader java.net.URLClassLoader @10272bbb)
```

With `buckets=50` and a `[5m]` window, the query works up to a 4h range (step ≤ ~4.8m) and fails from 4.5h (step ~5.4m) upward. The same queries over a `counter`-typed field work at every range. On 9.6/9.7 snapshots, the gauge queries also work at every range.

| 9.5.3, `sum(<fn>(requests[5m]))`, `buckets=50` | 1h | 4h | 4.5h | 6h | 24h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rate`, gauge field | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `irate`, gauge field | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `increase`, gauge field | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `rate`, counter field | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 9.6.0 / 9.7.0-SNAPSHOT, all three over the gauge field | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

**Why this matters:** Prometheus remote-write into `/_prometheus/api/v1/write` stores untyped exporter counters as gauges. Any Prometheus-style dashboard panel `rate(x[5m])` over such a metric therefore fails in Kibana once the time picker is set wider than about 4 hours.

**Expected:** the query returns values, or a clear error, rather than an internal `ClassCastException`.

**Possibly related:** #151974 / #156180 fixed the same exception for `delta`/`idelta` with narrow windows and were backported to 9.5.2. This case still reproduces on 9.5.3. The 9.6 time-series window rework in #155520 may be what fixed it on 9.6, but I have not bisected. If so, a backport or a targeted 9.5 fix would help.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a time-series index with a gauge field and 24h of monotonically increasing samples (+10 every 30s):

```
PUT gauge-rate-repro
{
  "settings": {
    "index.mode": "time_series",
    "index.routing_path": ["host"],
    "index.time_series.start_time": "<now-25h>",
    "index.time_series.end_time": "<now+1h>"
  },
  "mappings": {
    "properties": {
      "@timestamp": {"type": "date"},
      "host": {"type": "keyword", "time_series_dimension": true},
      "requests": {"type": "double", "time_series_metric": "gauge"}
    }
  }
}

POST gauge-rate-repro/_bulk?refresh=true
{"create":{}}
{"@timestamp":"<now-24h>","host":"a","requests":10}
{"create":{}}
{"@timestamp":"<now-24h+30s>","host":"a","requests":20}
... (one document every 30s up to now, +10 each; 2880 documents)
```

2. Query a 4h range. This works:

```
POST _query
{"query": "PROMQL index=gauge-rate-repro start=\"<now-4h>\" end=\"<now>\" buckets=50 value=(sum(rate(requests[5m])))"}
```

3. Query a 6h range. This fails with the `class_cast_exception` above:

```
POST _query
{"query": "PROMQL index=gauge-rate-repro start=\"<now-6h>\" end=\"<now>\" buckets=50 value=(sum(rate(requests[5m])))"}
```

4. Recreate the index with `"time_series_metric": "counter"` and step 3 succeeds.

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

issue.body:
Closes #162319
Closes #159710
Closes #163279
Closes #163280

The PromQL delta() csv-spec tests intermittently returned slightly wrong values for the first 10m bucket. DeltaAggregator keeps only the first and last sample of a series plus a valuesSeen count, but append() silently dropped any sample whose timestamp fell between the current first and last without counting it, while combine() assumed both samples it appends from a partial state were counted. When doc partitioning or partial emits split a series across partial states and an earlier partial was merged before a later one, valuesSeen ended up short, which changed averageSampleInterval and therefore the capped start-gap extrapolation in evaluateFinal. Only the first bucket was affected because that is where the gap to the window start exceeds the cap. Same-timestamp ties from multi-valued samples were likewise decided by arrival order.

This PR makes append() count every value and break same-timestamp ties towards the larger value at both ends, so the state is the same regardless of input or merge order; on the usual single-driver path the result is unchanged, so no csv-spec expectations move. It adds DeltaDoubleAggregatorTests covering out-of-order raw input, both partial merge orders, multi-valued ties and random partitions, and unmutes the multi-node test.

Related (same root cause; stay muted until 9.5/9.4 backports land, do not close on this merge):
- #162369
- #162371
- #162373

issue.title: PromQL: add sort_by_label and sort_by_label_desc

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Pull request authored by a developer outside the Elasticsearch team

labels.name: user-67ce657a/repo-12a517a4
labels.description: PromQL support for Elastic

issue.body:
Adds PromQL `sort_by_label` / `sort_by_label_desc`: identity-preserving instant-vector ordering by label values in [natural order](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/44ae3e8aedfeb305a462029a26c667f3d3f418ca/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/expression/promql/function/NaturalSortKey.java#L33-L41). Requested labels are materialized on an open header and skipped on a closed one. Tie-break is `_timeseries` when present, otherwise the remaining labels in label-name order.

`PROMQL_SORT_BY_LABEL` covers both functions; they ship together.

## Known gaps vs Prometheus

**Only the outermost sort is applied.** Because the ordering is injected above `TimeSeriesCollapse`, only the ordering of the outermost function can reach the rows the client sees. A nested call such as `abs(sort_by_label(metric, "pod"))` is rejected with `[sort_by_label] is only supported at the top-level at this time`. The check lives in #158931 and covers all four sort functions; for these two it matters more, because a nested call would also have exposed the label column that is materialized internally to bind the ordering to.

Prometheus accepts such calls, and the ordering really is observable there: for an instant query its engine [takes an explicit shortcut so as not to change the sort order](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/v3.15.0/promql/engine.go#L1578-L1579), and instant-vector results are never re-sorted afterwards. So this is a current limitation on our side rather than a deliberate semantic difference, and there is a `TODO` at the rejection site.

**Range results are not ordered by labels.** Prometheus sorts every range (matrix) result by labels, and its own warning says a sort is ineffective for range queries "since results are always ordered by labels". We emit an equivalent warning, but we return range results in their input order, with no label ordering. That part is pre-existing in the Prometheus API layer — the range plan builder adds no ordering — so it is not introduced by this PR and wants tracking separately.

**Tie-break edge cases.** When the requested labels are equal, Prometheus orders by the full label set ([`labels.Compare`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/v3.5.0/model/labels/labels_stringlabels.go#L325)). We approximate it, and the result differs only in these cases:
- Closed header: a series missing a label that is followed by a later label sorts first here, where Prometheus sorts it last. Non-string label columns (`ip`, numeric, `boolean` dimensions) are ordered by their native type rather than as strings.
- Open header: the tie-break is the `_timeseries` JSON string. It differs when one label set is the other plus extra trailing labels, for values that are prefixes of each other followed by a space or `!`, for unquoted numeric values, and for stored (non-synthetic) source, whose key order may not be by label name.

Matching exactly would need a dedicated sort key encoding the whole label set, which is out of scope for an experimental function.

Note that the warning itself is not a difference: Prometheus has emitted one since 3.12, so the previously documented "Prometheus discards it silently" was out of date and is corrected here.

issue.body:
## What

When `BinaryOperator.canonicalize()` is called, binary operator's commutative children expressions (e.g. `TODOUBLE($1) + TODOUBLE($2)`) are sorted by semantic hash. 

For `Attribute`, `semanticHash()` returns non-deterministic value across JVM runs / instances. I.e. it depends on how many attributes were created before this expression.

It makes canonical order inconsistent and golden tests flaky. Also if for some reason the plan needs to run on multiple nodes the optimizer can fail to recognize equivalent commutative expressions as equal. 

## Fix

Use deterministic key for expression sorting.

Closes #157912 & #157827
